subject: Request: EU-only hosting attestation and private endpoint evidence
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsafe-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Schmidt <nora.schmidt@medsafe-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: EU hosting & private endpoint evidence request

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and security review for a pilot, our InfoSec team needs a concise evidence packet showing that Redwood can: 1) guarantee EU-only data residency for processing and storage, 2) provide a private endpoint (VPC peering/private link) for dedicated traffic, and 3) demonstrate KMS key separation for tenant encryption in EU regions.

Concretely, please include:
- A one-page attestation we can share with our legal team stating EU-only processing for pinned deployments
- Network diagram showing the private endpoint and peering configuration (labels for azs and subnets appreciated)
- Snapshot of SOC 2 scope statement relevant to hosting locations and KMS use
- Your CAIQ/SIG responses for anything relevant to data residency, key management, and private connectivity

We'd like to move quickly — can you get an initial packet by EOD Tuesday (two business days)? Also let me know who on your team I can follow up with about MAP/rollout steps.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Director, IT Security
Medsafe Analytics

Attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsafe-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: EU hosting & private endpoint evidence request

Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. I can own the coordination and will get you an initial packet by end of day Tuesday. Looping in Karthik (security/infra) and Marissa (solutions) so they can attach the technical artifacts you asked for.

Two quick clarifying Qs so we send the right docs:
1) When you say "EU-only for pinned deployments," do you need an SLA-level written commitment for the pilot (i.e., contract appendix), or is a technical attestation + runbook sufficient for your internal review?
2) Do you want KMS to be customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed with tenant isolation? We support both; we'll include both options and recommended timelines.

If you prefer a short MAP (mutual action plan) template, Marissa can draft one for signature. We can also prepare a DocuSign-ready MAP if that helps procurement.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsafe-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T11:23:00-04:00
Subject: Re: EU hosting & private endpoint evidence request

Liam, Jordan —

Thanks — here is the concise technical evidence and statements for Medsafe's review. I'll summarize first, then point to the attached artifacts.

Summary statements (short, shareable):
- EU-only processing: For Dedicated or Private deployments, Redwood can pin all customer compute and storage to EU regions (currently eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). We maintain strict routing and storage controls; control plane metadata (non-sensitive) may transit control endpoints in other regions unless requested otherwise. We will provide a contract appendix to bind EU-only processing for the pilot if required.
- Private endpoint: We support PrivateLink-style private endpoints and VPC peering for Dedicated capacity and Private deployments. Traffic carrying tenant request/response payloads remains on private connections to the extent of the peering configuration; we include an operator-runbook for setup and maintenance.
- KMS & encryption: We support both Redwood-managed CMKs partitioned per-customer (EU key partitioning) and customer-managed keys (BYOK) via external KMS/HSM integrations. For high-regulation customers we recommend BYOK + customer-scoped key policies.

Attachments included (see files):
- runbook_vpc_eu_20260920.pdf  — operator runbook: peering steps, ACLs, route tables, failover
- vpc_diagram_azs.png — simplified AZ/subnet diagram for PrivateLink + dedicated pool
- caiq_responses_medsafe.xlsx — filtered CAIQ with residency, KMS, network controls highlighted
- soc2_snapshot_2026Q2.pdf — SOC 2 scope summary; shows Hosting/Encryption sections and test coverage (redaction applied)
- map_draft_medsafe.docx — draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we can convert to DocuSign

Key technical notes (short):
- Isolation: Dedicated pools run on tenant-isolated GPU fleets; we maintain workload-level tenant tags and network-level filters.
- Cache/KV: KV cache can be localized to EU-only nodes for pinned deployments; we provide cache-clear runbook steps for incident scenarios.
- Logs and audit: Audit logs (control plane and operator actions) are available for the EU deployment with configurable retention; we include a sample export process in the runbook.
- Fallbacks: If Dedicated capacity is unavailable in EU region, we can configure policy to fail open (reject requests) or fail over to a colocated EU-compatible fallback — we will not route to non-EU regions for pinned launches without explicit acceptance.

Next steps: Jordan/Marissa — we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough with Medsafe on Thursday to walk the runbook and the diagram. Liam — if procurement prefers an executed MAP, tell us and we'll produce a DocuSign bundle.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_vpc_eu_20260920.pdf, vpc_diagram_azs.png, caiq_responses_medsafe.xlsx, soc2_snapshot_2026Q2.pdf, map_draft_medsafe.docx

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medsafe-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Schmidt <nora.schmidt@medsafe-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T13:44:00-04:00
Subject: Re: EU hosting & private endpoint evidence request

Karthik/Jordan —

This is great — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear artifacts. The runbook and the diagram answer the majority of our technical questions. A couple of asks before we close:
- Can you convert the MAP draft to a DocuSign-ready package and include expected timelines for provisioning (pilot provisioning SLA)?
- For the SOC 2 snapshot, we need a signed letter (short) that specifies that EU hosting is in-scope for the SOC 2 coverage you provided — if you can provide that by COB Friday that would help our legal team.

If you like, Nora and I can take the MAP and propose dates for the pilot steps; happy to pick Thursday for the walkthrough.

Thanks again —
Liam
Director, IT Security
Medsafe Analytics
